newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition members of Democrat party have turned the Parliament policy debate into a no-confidence forum against Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, questioning his past handling of a border dispute area with Laos, business deals in the Cambodian border area and his close relationship with the Burmese junta. The fierce attack on the prime minister was made yesterday. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- A group of 500 people, including academics and military officers, have shown their support for Police Maj Gen Seri Temiyavej, who is under investigation for his allegations of police involvement in illegal gambling operations. The group says it will stand by the officer and urged him to continue fighting graft and corruption. (THE NATION)

- Tigers on the loose in Saraburi province are being pursued by a 200-strong contingent made up of a local police task force, zoologists and rescue workers - but their fear of accidentally shooting each other has hampered the much-publicised hunt. The tigers began their carnivorous rampage on Saturday by preying on residents' cattle and have continued to feast on the fowl and pets in the area ever since. (THE NATION)

- Government measures to solve the property slump are likely to cause a chain reaction on the whole economy, financiers and developers say. A senior banker says it is not practical for developers to raise funds through a capital increase as they are hampered both by oversupply and liquidity problems. (BANGKOK POST)

- The retail price of diesel fuel will be raised by 15 satang per litre in the next few days because the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) can no longer shoulder the burden of increased crude oil prices. PTT earlier said it was absorbing a loss of some 20 satang a litre in order to maintain the price of diesel. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand says a study is underway to improve the tabulation of the Minimum Retail Rate (MRR) in order to help retail borrowers. The study is expected to be finalised next year and the central bank will consult with commercial banks should any changes to the calculation of MRR be necessary. The current MRR is too close to the Minimum Lending Rate and Minimum Overdraft Rate which is deemed inappropiate, especially for retail borrowers who shoulder higher interest costs than large borrowers. (BUSINESS DAY)
